title: Decoding edge value
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with alphabet $\text{Fin}(q)$, let $T$ be a table assigning a Boolean function to each vertex, let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, and choose a default label $a_0\in\text{Fin}(q)$. For a vertex $v$ and a neighbor $w$ of $v$, the decoding edge value is the candidate decoding edge value formed from the candidates decoded from $T$ at parameter $\varepsilon$, using $a_0$.
hypotheses_covered: A regular unique game $G$ with alphabet size $q$
A Boolean-function table indexed by vertices
A vertex and a neighbor of that vertex
caveat: The candidate-decoding and edge-value definitions are absent, so their precise numerical meaning is unavailable.
